newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes end higher amid ANS deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes end higher amid ANS deals.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices ended higher late Wednesday after benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose and differentials firmed following two afternoon deals.
Activity picked up as BP America, the dominant producer of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, sold full cargoes at $1.60 and 1.53 off February WTI.
The buyer of the $1.60 cargo expected the shipment to arrive at their Hawaii refinery in mid-February.
The buyer at $1.53 was not available for comment.
